gen-fs-quilon-gf-roboto: Editorial in spirit, Quilon swells and thins its strokes with a medium-low contrast and leaves generous counters inside its tall letters. And Roboto, a sans-serif, keeps its rounds open and its capitals close to lowercase height.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-ruda: Commanding up top, Quilon rises and thins in a gentle swell, while Ruda draws a wire-like sans-serif line with wide-mouthed rounds. Quilon earns its keep on big, short lines.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-saira: Saira reads cleanly, each s showing a see-through gap and its rounded letters stretching toward the top line. Quilon's reed-pen swelling is the standout, lending an editorial, commanding edge.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-sarpanch: Editorial swagger up top, friendly compactness below. The standout is the contrast between Quilon's sturdy, slightly heavier thick strokes and Sarpanch's low-contrast line with its clearly open e.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-sen: Sen reads in a rope-like line, tall in the lowercase, its curves ending before they turn inward. And Quilon does what Sen doesn't, bringing a light touch of modulation and an editorial, commanding voice.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-sintony: Quilon's stroke swells and thins in a slow, steady rhythm. Sintony then supplies a chunky, tall midzone and low contrast, so headings and text sit together smoothly with no clogged curves.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-sofia-sans: Quilon brings medium-contrast strokes and large open counters, while Sofia Sans stays in one steady thickness with rounded, open-sided letters. Paragraphs of it should move along smoothly, tall and stencil-crisp.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-sofia-sans-semi-condens: Stencil-cut and sign-shop crisp, Sofia Sans Semi Condensed holds one line width, its lowercase nearly matching the capitals in height. Quilon earns its keep large and brief, with a sensible stroke shift.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-stack-sans-notch: Commanding and editorial, Quilon swells gently through its rounded letters, with open counters in tall forms. Stack Sans Notch, drawn like bent wire, can go a touch smaller since its big-bodied lowercase and open curves stay legible.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-stack-sans-text: Modern in feel, Stack Sans Text holds a marker-like line with curve endings kept well apart. But its real strength is the meeting with Quilon, whose medium-low stroke contrast adds an editorial, commanding lift.
